analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal has an admirable 9-year earnings track record and negligible debt, but at 74x earnings and 4.75x book, Mr. Market is pricing in a quality business at a speculative premium far beyond any margin of safety. The Graham Number (approx. INR 264) is less than one-third of the current price of INR 940.
key_strengths: Unbroken profitability since at least 2016, meeting Graham's multi-year earnings continuity requirement
Debt/Equity of 0.08 — balance sheet virtually debt-free, survivability in downturns is not a concern
OCF positive all 5 of 5 measured years; operating cash flow broadly tracks reported earnings
key_risks: P/E of 74.2x is nearly 5x Graham's maximum threshold of 15x — price embeds extraordinary growth expectations
Net profit fell sharply to INR 299 Cr in FY2025 from INR 476 Cr in FY2024 — a 37% collapse that calls into question the earnings quality
Other income turned negative (-23 Cr) in FY2025 after sizable contributions in prior years, suggesting non-recurring gains had inflated historical profits
red_flags: Graham Number ~INR 264 vs market price INR 940 — trading at a 256% premium to intrinsic value by Graham's formula
P/B of 4.75x versus Graham's ceiling of 1.5x — nearly all market capitalisation is goodwill and future expectations, not tangible assets
FY2025 net profit drop of 37% with simultaneously negative other income suggests a potential structural or one-time impairment that has not been explained
analysis.detailed_analysis: Carborundum Universal is a legitimate industrial business with a real moat in abrasives, ceramics, and electrominerals built over 70 years. Its balance sheet is clean (D/E 0.08, cash INR 378 Cr) and its revenue has compounded at a respectable 10.8% over nine years. From Graham's standpoint, this is a company one could study with interest — but not buy at the current price. With a Graham Number of approximately INR 264 (based on FY2025 EPS of ~INR 15.7 and BVPS of ~INR 197) against a market price of INR 940, the stock commands a 256% premium to the formula's implied fair value — there is no margin of safety whatsoever. The FY2025 profit collapse from INR 476 Cr to INR 299 Cr is particularly troubling; the intelligent investor demands consistent earning power, not volatile results hidden behind prior-year other income. Until the price corrects dramatically or earnings recover sustainably, this remains firmly in speculative territory by my standards.
